name: Gujarati

ancestors.notes: Descent via Shauraseni Apabhraṃśa / Old Gujarati
Persian influence through Mughal period and Parsi community

notes: Standard Gujarati (Gujarat, India). Distinct Gujarati script derived from Devanagari. ⟨ળ⟩ = [ɭ] retroflex lateral is a phoneme (unlike most IA). Four-way laryngeal contrast retained. Short /ə/ deleted in word-final position (schwa deletion, encoded as GU_SCHWA_FINAL_* allophone_rules: Mistry 1997: 653-654; Cardona & Jain 2003). ⟨આ⟩/⟨ા⟩ (long a) is phonetically a back unrounded [ɑ], not a lengthened front [aː] (Mistry 1997: 654; Cardona 1965: 12) — contrasts with the deletable inherent schwa [ə], no separate length mark needed. ⟨ર⟩ /r/ is phonetically an alveolar tap [ɾ] (Mistry 1997: 656), not a trill.

sources.author: Mistry, P. J.
sources.title: Gujarati Phonology
sources.publisher: in Kaye, A.S. (ed.) Phonologies of Asia and Africa, Eisenbrauns
sources.notes: Word-final schwa deletion (pp. 653-654) and /r/ realized as an alveolar tap [ɾ]; the source for the GU_SCHWA_FINAL_* rules and the r->ɾ allophone.

allophone_rules.notes: Word-final schwa deletion. Gujarati, like Hindi, does not pronounce the inherent vowel of a word-final consonant letter (Cardona & Suthar 2003: 665-666; Mistry 1997: 653-654). word_initial=false protects a monosyllabic one-consonant-letter word whose schwa is its only vowel.
